title: Food systems transformation would reshape global agriculture.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the only data file on Zenodo record 17570720 (manuscript_data_upload_101125.csv, 33.3 MB, CC-BY-4.0). It has 407,394 rows and 10 columns: model (10 economic models, e.g. GLOBIOM, IMPACT, MAgPIE), scenario (5: BAU, BAU_DIET, BAU_PROD, BAU_WAST, EL2), region (14), variable (13, e.g. AREA, PROD, EMIS, YILD), item (10 commodity groups), unit (17 strings), year (2020-2050), percent_change_from_2020, percent_change_from_BAU_2050. No duplicate keys; about 4,700 missing values in each value column. Values are only percent changes, not absolute quantities. Zenodo record 14876855 holds a single figure notebook.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the values come from scenario simulations by a ten-model ensemble of global economic models (abstract and data availability statement). The FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization) and HYDE historical land-use data are external and were not opened.

a1_downloadable.note: One 33 MB CSV on Zenodo, open, CC-BY-4.0; downloaded and parsed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in the file: there is no measured outcome column. The only numeric columns are simulated percent changes, so any 'label' would be one economic model's projection, chosen by us.

a3_inputs_present.note: Scenario, region, commodity, variable and year are all categorical columns in the file; no lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: A unit column exists, though mixed within some variables (e.g. prices as USD/t, USD/t dm, index 2014=1, 2015 USD/t); values are percent changes, so units matter little.

a5_enough_rows.note: 407,394 rows counted, but they are 10 models x 5 scenarios x 14 regions x ~13 variables x 31 years, so the number of independent units is tiny.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The 10 models and 5 scenarios in the file match the paper's description; the paper gives no row count to compare against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Every value in the file is the output of a simulation model (scenario projections to 2050), not a physical measurement. Any ML model trained on it would only emulate those economic models; it's circular by construction.

integration.join_key: region + commodity + year (would need mapping between model aggregate regions and FAO countries)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not pursued: the study's own data are projections, so a join only compares one set of models against history, which the model teams already do.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained on this would only reproduce what ten economic simulators project for five stylised 2050 scenarios. It would say nothing measured about agriculture.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use scenario, region, commodity and year to predict the projected percent change in agricultural land, production or emissions by 2050.
plain_idea.train_on: Each row is one combination of economic model, scenario, region, variable, commodity and year; there are 407,394 rows, but they come from only 10 models and 5 scenarios.
plain_idea.predict: The percent change from 2020 or from business-as-usual in 2050. The true answer is itself a simulation output from global economic models, not a measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little value: an emulator of these ten simulators adds nothing their authors can't already compute. The spread between models is the interesting part, and the paper already reports it.

ml_idea: Considered: emulate the ten-model ensemble's projected 2050 changes from scenario/region/commodity descriptors, or predict model disagreement. Rejected because every target is a simulation output (A8) and no measured label exists (A2).

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 33 MB CSV that loaded in pandas in seconds; nothing was timed beyond loading.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether any column is a measurement rather than a simulation output. Done: none is.

verdict_reason: Opened the single 407,394-row Zenodo CSV. Every value is a simulated percent change from ten economic models under five 2050 scenarios, so there is no measured label (A2) and any target is another model's output (A8). Existing-model search was skipped after Part A failed. It also isn't really a biology ML dataset.
